content.title: Course Details Page
content.prompt: Build a "Course Details" page for a fictional course called Frontend Foundations. Requirements: a page title; a short course description; a table of the three module names and their durations; an unordered list of three prerequisites; and a labeled sign-up form (name and email, with a submit button). Choose the HTML elements yourself based on what each part of the content actually is — no element types are specified for you beyond what's implied by the content.
content.instructions: No starter structure is provided beyond an empty body. Plan your regions before writing markup.

testCases.description: Page has exactly one top-level heading
Contains a table with a header row and at least three module rows
Contains an unordered list with at least three prerequisites
Contains a form with two associated labels and a submit control
testCases.assertion: document.querySelectorAll('form label[for]').length === 2 && document.querySelector('form button[type=submit], form input[type=submit]') !== null

content.title: Self-Check Without Hints
content.prompt: Before checking any reference answer, review your own Course Details page against these questions, honestly: Does every form label have a matching for/id pair? Does your heading structure skip any levels? Would every image (if you added one) make sense to someone who can't see it? Below is a page with issues of exactly this kind planted in it — find and fix them without hints.
content.bugDescription: The heading jumps from h1 to h3, skipping h2, and the label has no for attribute matching the input's id.
fixRequirements: Heading should be h2, not h3
Label needs for="student-name" to match the input's id
